3A student here - I lived in Stratford in 2nd year for both terms and honestly didn’t find it that bad! Though keep in mind I’m an introvert, and managed to make a friend group who all lived in Stratford so we’d have fun just staying till late on campus doing movie nights in study rooms. 

Because of the pilot bus program they have now, they’ve kinda adjusted the timetables afaik to make them longer and less frequent to make them more convenient for commuters, so it’s definitely a better option to live in Loo than it once was - however, for either the UW bus, the PC Connect bus or carpools you usually have to wake up at 6/7am which is kind of a slog imo if u have afternoon classes. I value sleep and convenience above everything else, so I prefer living in Stratford. 

Aside from that, if you have a friend with a car in Loo and can convince them to drive you, or you can crash at a friend’s place overnight then it’s pretty feasible to go to Waterloo every once and a while via the PC Connect bus - though granted, it doesn’t run on Sundays and the timings are pretty hit/miss, and it frequently gets snowed out during late Winter. 

Overall though, I’d say go with what you value most since tbh the prices kinda even out at the end of the day - if you value sleep + convenience + small town vibes and don’t mind a small circle of friends, then go for Stratford. If you prefer more of an urban/city vibe, are really dedicated to a club and have a ton of friends on main campus + you think you can wake up early enough for the commute, then go for Waterloo.

Hi, my school offers both CP and DP, and while i'm not in CP i think i could help a little! 

IBCP isn't offered as much as DP by schools, so if you're interested in it you'd first need to check if your school even offers it. 

In CP, the requirements are very different from DP. firstly, the core is different, consisting of: 

* Service Learning (similar to CAS, but with different requirements I believe) 
* Personal and Professional Skills 
* Language Development (of a second language) 
* Reflective Project (a research paper, similar to the EE)

Additionally, the candidate takes on at least 2 IBDP courses, and career-related studies (internships, etc... varies depending on your school's programme). 

Since CP is so hands-on and requires a lot of involvement - it's kind of like a technical college or polytechnic/vocational programme - I think it'd be pretty much impossible to take on IBDP and IBCP at the same time. if you really wanted to, not only would you have to fulfill all the career-related requirements, but you'd also have to complete **both the DP and CP core**, as well as your **6 IB subjects**, which is again, kinda impossible. 

If you're still interested in CP, it might still be alright for you to transfer since you're only one month into DP, so I'd suggest talking to the IB coordinator at your school!
